title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/analysis issues in the archive materially constrain inference: (1) execution used shared-generation semantics that invalidate the preregistered independent-per-condition power assumptions, and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit under the executed semantics and artifacts. We release authoritative archived artifacts and recommend independent-per-condition reruns, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model tests, and broader verifier coverage to evaluate operational value beyond the executed setting.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) can improve NetOps productivity but creates operational risk: stochastic generators sometimes produce syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate reachability, workflow, or security invariants. Prior work therefore frequently places deterministic validators between generation and execution and, in many proposals, couples validators with iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to deployment.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to answer a focused operational question: does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to a baseline generator, when evaluated on a public synthetic NetOps task bank under frozen execution semantics? The study (preregistration id: c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) used gpt-5-mini as the generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the oracle. The preregistration and execution artifacts are archived and authoritative for all reported numbers (preregistration SHA recorded in the archive). Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation on N = 240 tasks; (2) transparent execution accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240) and that every generation satisfied the verifier (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); and (4) operationally grounded recommendations and reproducible next steps to evaluate GVR under conditions that restore discordance potential and adversarial sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
We situate this experiment relative to three strands of literature: (i) LLM failure modes and hallucination in code and structured-output generation, which motivates mechanical validators; (ii) generate–verify–repair and constraint-based decoding techniques that improve syntactic and some semantic properties in prior case studies; and (iii) NetOps-specific verifier research and intent-translation systems that emphasize verifier-driven evaluation and human oversight.

Nearest-work comparison (representative, concise):
- NetConfEval / intent-translation studies (e.g., NetConfEval-like evaluations, 2024–2025): benchmarked LLMs for configuration tasks; typically report per-task accuracy but not preregistered paired GVR confirmatory designs. Our run differs by preregistration, paired design, and deterministic reconciliation on a synthetic verifier-checked bank.
- GVR and hybrid repair reports (generate–verify–repair case studies, 2025–2026): show improvements on mechanically checkable properties (compilation, tests) but are often single-repo or single-benchmark case studies. Our contribution is a preregistered paired confirmatory test with explicit estimands and archived analysis artifacts.
- Intent-based NetOps prototypes (Confucius, MeshAgent, INTA, 2024–2025): integrate LLMs with domain validators and operator workflows. These systems motivate our verifier-centered estimands; we differ by executing a frozen paired experiment that isolates GVR’s incremental verifier-detectable effect under bounded repair and shared-generation semantics.

References for the nearest-work matrix are drawn from the verified bibliography in the archived evidence bundle; see cited_record_ids for the precise records used in comparison.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study preregistration (c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) defined the primary estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the paired difference in proportion of verifier-detected semantic violations (GVR minus baseline), computed with the frozen executor paired_binary_analysis_v1. Two prespecified primary comparisons were registered: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding (Bonferroni family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025).

Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory sample N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial frozen execution semantics recorded prior to generation included generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); maximum_model_calls budget = 480. The execution manifest (archived) records planned_episode_count = 480 and completed_episode_count = 480.

Task bank and oracle: The synthetic task bank encodes initial device states, workflow policies, and required sequences; the deterministic validator implements pybatfish-style checks that return structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule used: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by validator v5. Representative task and validator traces are archived in execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Analysis plan and preregistered power: The preregistration targeted a 10 percentage-point absolute paired reduction with N = 240 under the independent-per-condition-generation assumption. Power calculations were frozen in the archive. The preregistered analyses used exact McNemar two-sided tests and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration also specified conservative missingness and contamination treatments; the execution artifacts record zero model-call or infrastructure failures.

Evidence-to-claim mapping (compact): the principal artifact-grounded claims below are mapped to archived artifact paths (full manifest with hashes is archived; see artifact appendix):
- Claim: All arms accepted every generated candidate (n11 = 240). Evidence: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv and execution/raw_results.jsonl.
- Claim: Model calls used = 240 and shared-generation semantics executed. Evidence: execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/model_configuration.json and execution/provider_calls/* (shared-initial traces).
- Claim: Paired estimate = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10k resamples, seed 1729). Evidence: analysis/results.json, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.
- Claim: Repair loop never applied (repair_applied = false for all episodes). Evidence: execution/scoring/task-*.json (validator_trace.validation_after.repair_applied) and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

(Full hash manifest and all per-episode artifacts are available in the archived execution/execution_manifest.json; see Artifact appendix.)
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 under shared-initial-candidate semantics. Analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms episode and provider-call accounting consistency.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (archived): contingency counts: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Marginal rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (method = paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and authoritative.

Repair and trigger diagnostics: For every episode validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count = 0 and validator_trace.repair_applied = false; thus the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied verifier predicates across the synthetic task bank. Representative scored artifacts are available under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ (examples included in the archive manifest).

Statistical interpretation: The absence of discordant within-pair outcomes (zero n10 and n01) renders the paired McNemar test degenerate: no within-pair disagreement exists to estimate differential effect. The observed p = 1.00 and the collapsed bootstrap CI are deterministic consequences of these counts and the preregistered analysis procedures. Crucially, the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; the executed shared-generation semantics (one shared candidate reused across arms) invalidated that assumption and the preregistered power argument for the run as executed.
sections.discussion:
Conservative operational interpretation: Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and for this synthetic task bank and verifier, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain this null outcome: (1) task/verifier alignment—this generator+prompt pairing produced candidates that already satisfied the validator predicates for the supplied tasks; and (2) sensitivity reduction by shared-generation semantics—reusing a single candidate across arms removes stochastic variation and removes the within-pair discordance that GVR could exploit.

Evaluation-practice implications: Demonstrating incremental value of GVR requires evaluation semantics aligned to inferential assumptions. If the goal is to measure whether GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under generator stochasticity, the experiment must permit independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks that reliably induce verifier failures, test multiple generator families and prompts, or expand the repair budget.

Relation to prior work: Our artifacts and null outcome align with literature that (a) recommends verifier-interposed pipelines to reduce mechanically checkable errors and (b) shows that measurable benefit depends on generator stochasticity, verifier coverage, and adversarial load. The present contribution is methodological: a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run with transparent reconciliation of preregistered assumptions and executed semantics and with archived artifacts enabling deterministic reruns under alternative generation semantics.

Threats to validity and unresolved procedural deviation: Internal validity is affected by the mismatch between preregistered independent-generation assumptions and executed shared-generation semantics. Construct validity is limited by verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes a subset of operational invariants. External validity is limited by a single generator (gpt-5-mini), synthetic tasks, and a single bounded repair budget (one attempt). A prespecified comparison (C vs B: GVR vs schema-constrained decoding) was listed in the preregistration but was not executed in the archived run; no recorded rationale appears in the manifest. These threats are documented in the archive and enumerated in the Limitations section.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. However, two execution/preregistration deviations materially constrain inference: (1) the shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison was not executed. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts and recommend deterministic reruns under independent-per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model comparisons, expanded repair budgets, and broader verifier coverage to robustly assess GVR’s operational value in NetOps contexts.

Artifact appendix (concise): The full execution and analysis manifest (including the complete per-artifact hash manifest) is archived (execution/execution_manifest.json, analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/scoring/*.json). These artifacts are authoritative for all reported numbers and enable deterministic reruns under alternate generation_semantics; see the archived manifest for complete file-level hashes and provider-call traces. For compactness we cite only key artifact paths in the main text; the full manifest contains exhaustive per-file hashes and provenance.

Reproducible next steps (archive-anchored): (1) rerun with independent_condition_generation = true using the same task manifest and RNG seeds to restore discordance potential; (2) inject adversarial/golden tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) to validate verifier sensitivity; (3) test additional generator families and prompts; (4) increase the repair budget and record repair-iteration distributions; (5) broaden verifier predicates or integrate formal-verification hybrids to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. The archived scripts and manifests provide the deterministic inputs required for these reruns. Contact the archive manifest to retrieve exact artifact lists for replication and extension (see Artifact appendix).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
